hook: Gold didn't move. Your price did.

editorial_brief.viewer_question: How can the rupee cost of gold rise when its dollar price stays flat?
editorial_brief.misconception: A flat dollar price means an unchanged rupee cost.
editorial_brief.mechanism: With a constant dollar value, more rupees per dollar increases the rupee equivalent.
editorial_brief.proof_plan: Show an illustrative $100 amount at 80 then 85 rupees per dollar: 8000 then 8500 rupees. Hold the dollar amount constant. Label all frames as illustration, not today's prices.
editorial_brief.boundary: Currency conversion only; not a jewellery quote, MCX fair value, current price, prediction or complete import-cost model.
editorial_brief.memory_check: Check gold and the rupee together.
editorial_brief.human_opening: A person sees a flat global gold headline but a higher rupee cost.
editorial_brief.primary_source: World Gold Council: Indian premium/discount methodology and gold-pricing primer; direct links in sources.
editorial_brief.voice_tone: Warm, concise female Indian-English narration, conversational rather than dramatic.

storyboard.copy:
Gold didn't move.
Your price did.
storyboard.narration: Gold stayed flat. Your rupee cost rose.
storyboard.visual: Immediate tactile gold close-up; the complete hook is visible on frame zero. A small illustration label prevents a live-price implication.

storyboard.copy:
A weaker rupee.
A higher rupee cost.
storyboard.narration: A weaker rupee makes the same dollar-priced gold cost more.
storyboard.visual: Fixed $100 tile; exchange-rate tile changes from 80 to 85. Computed rupee equivalent changes from 8000 to 8500. Before and after remain visible together; no market chart.

storyboard.narration: Same gold. Different rupee cost. Check both.
storyboard.visual: Return to the same bangle, holding the two-variable takeaway without a sales end card.

voiceover: Gold stayed flat. Your rupee cost rose. A weaker rupee makes the same dollar-priced gold cost more. Same gold. Different rupee cost. Check both.
caption:
The gold can stay the same while its rupee equivalent changes.

Illustration only: $100 × ₹80/$ = ₹8,000; $100 × ₹85/$ = ₹8,500. These are invented round numbers to isolate currency conversion, not today's prices or the price of the pictured bangle. Local taxes, premiums, purity and retail costs are outside this example.

Mechanism: World Gold Council, Indian premium/discount methodology: https://www.gold.org/sites/default/files/downloads/2019-02/Indian_premium-discount_methodology.pdf
